reason: A is the stronger proposal because it tests a specific, novel processing intervention against a composition-matched baseline and explicitly links verified boundary serration to creep and corrosion outcomes, whereas B largely repeats the cited Mo-alloying study and even conflates its at.% addition with wt.%. A remains high-risk because serration in the prior alloy depended on γ′ precipitates absent from the proposed alloy, while Mo/Cr-rich σ-phase formation and boundary segregation could instead impair ductility or corrosion.
